# GitHub API fixtures

These files, except `pull-request.json` and `release-latest.json` (captured answers, see their rows), are **not captured from GitHub.** They are reference-built from GitHub's documentation and its OpenAPI
description (<https://github.com/github/rest-api-description>, `descriptions/api.github.com/api.github.com.json`),
because no real sample of the answers was available when the GitHub App step of the setup wizard was built (decision
0017, Product Manager's decision; the Telegram fixtures were built the same way, decision 0016). The App ID, slug,
owner, client id and client secret are the documentation's invented example values; the private key is the
documentation's example key, which is public and grants nothing.

| File                                         | Follows (sections of the description)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `manifest-conversion.json`                   | `components.examples.integration-from-manifest.value`, the example answer of `POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions` (status 201), **verbatim**: `pem` is PKCS#1 (`-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----`). Its `owner` (`login` `github`, `type` `User`) is inconsistent with the organization URLs beside it, so the owner is reference-built                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `manifest-conversion-not-found.json`         | `components.responses.not_found` (status 404, schema `basic-error`: `message`, `documentation_url`, `status`), written from the schema                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `manifest-conversion-validation-failed.json` | `components.responses.validation_failed_simple` (status 422, schema `validation-error-simple`: `message`, `documentation_url`), written from the schema                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `manifest-conversion-pkcs8.json`             | `{"pkcs8": "<PEM>"}`: the key of `manifest-conversion.json` converted with `openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -nocrypt` (OpenSSL 3.0.13), the expected output of `toPkcs8Pem`. Not an answer of GitHub                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `installation-token.json`                    | `components.examples.installation-token.value`, the example answer of `POST /app/installations/{installation_id}/access_tokens` (status 201), **verbatim**: the token `ghs_16C7e42F292c6912E7710c838347Ae178B4a` and `expires_at` `2016-07-11T22:14:10Z` are the documentation's invented values                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `installations.json`                         | `components.examples.base-installation-items.value`, the example answer of `GET /app/installations` (status 200), **verbatim**: one installation of a `User` account with `repository_selection` `selected`; other account forms and long lists are built in the tests from it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `pull-request.json`                          | **Captured, not reference-built:** the answer of `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/77` (HTTP 200, `gh api`, 2026-10-19), a merged pull request (`draft` `false`), anonymized as `.squad/project.md` (_Fixtures from real deliveries_) prescribes: logins, ids, `node_id`s, URLs, repository name, homepage, description, topics, commit SHAs, branch name, title and body are replaced by invented values; structure, field set, types and `draft` are untouched. The draft variant is built in the test from it |
| `rsa-key-sizes.json`                         | `{"bits4096": "<PEM>", "bits4104": "<PEM>"}`: two RSA keys of exactly 4096 and of 4104 bits as PKCS#8 PEM, generated with `openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA` (OpenSSL 3.0.13) for the key size limit of `importSigningKey`. Not an answer of GitHub; the keys are throwaway and grant nothing                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `release-latest.json`                        | **Captured, not reference-built:** the answer of `GET /repos/LarsLaskowski/Seluna/releases/latest` (HTTP 200, `gh api`, 2026-10-21), the latest full release `v0.4.0` (`prerelease` `false`), anonymized as `.squad/project.md` (_Fixtures from real deliveries_) prescribes: owner, repository, logins, ids, `node_id`s and URLs are replaced by invented values; structure, field set, types, `tag_name`, flags and dates are untouched                                                                       |

Because they share the documentation's assumptions, tests built on them cannot catch a deviation of the real API from
the description. Replace them with captured answers (secrets removed) once the live check on a deployed copy yields
some; a deviation found by the live check is a new issue, not a silent edit of these files.
